source_revisions.sqlite: SQLite bundled by rusqlite 0.35 (version printed in runs)

build: cargo +stable build --release --locked --example kv_bench at each named revision

machine.filesystem_backing: Unknown; overlay behavior and physical storage are not independently verified.

limitations: Closed-loop, in-process benchmark with 250 cached keys and 64-byte values; it does not represent all databases or production workloads.

SQLite exposes SQL, transactions and features absent from the prototype. The workloads and requested sync behavior are similar, but internal semantics and reliability guarantees are not equivalent or independently validated.
The old engine requests sync per mutation; the new engine allows multiple concurrent independent mutations to share a sync. Both return success only after their data is covered by a sync.
Runs share virtual CPU and an overlay filesystem with unknown backing; there is no isolated disk or controlled CPU clock and results can vary.
Process CPU time and peak RSS cover startup, key initialization, measurement and cleanup; the benchmark binary includes both engines, so RSS is not the standalone engine footprint.
Latency is closed-loop and does not capture offered-load latency under overload; no network, cold cache, crash, power-loss, large data, multi-tenant or competitor-wide claims are established.
The Linux max-RSS high-water mark may include the Python runner before exec; these RSS values are not a reliable standalone memory comparison.
